items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The mission, payload, orbit phases, organization, and early design/concept-selection lifecycle are described in detail.
evidence: The Biofilm Onboard Radiation Exposure Assessment Lab In Space (BOREALIS) mission is a 6U CubeSat initiative funded by the Italian Space Agency under the ALCOR program
The 10-month mission includes a 3-month LEO phase for lower-radiation studies, followed by an MEO phase
Regarding the design process, starting from the scientific objectives of the mission, the mission requirements and constraints have been identified

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?
items.rationale: The study provides the AD structure, mission concepts, MAU/cost equations, weights rationale, input data appendix, simulations, and tools; it does not use a formal SysML language, but the analytical method is sufficiently described for comparison.
evidence: The multiple mission concepts were evaluated using Multi-Attribute Utility (MAU) and cost functions to assess their performance and expense.
The model incorporates normalized data for each variable based on the performance of each subsystem in the reference mission concept [Annex A].
In this Appendix, the input data to the model to evaluate the BOREALIS mission concepts are reported
Valispace is chosen as the main software platform to manage all mission design data.

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Key outcomes are linked to the tradespace model, ADs, Monte Carlo simulations, sensitivity analysis, and planned integrated design model.
evidence: By integrating parametrized tradespace evaluation, Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis into the system engineering process, this study demonstrated the effectiveness of a data-driven approach to guide the satellite configuration.
A concrete example of how this methodology impacted the BOREALIS design is evident in the evolution of the propulsion subsystem.
The integration of sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations added value to the design process, enabling informed decision making and enhancing the reliability of the chosen architecture.

items.question: Is evidence provided for claimed outcomes, such as metrics, baseline comparison, case-study results, executable simulation results, model checks, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration/test results, or flight/operational data?
items.rationale: Evidence consists of case-study model outputs, quantitative utility/cost tradespaces, propulsion and radiation simulations, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, sensitivity analysis, and reference architecture benchmarks, though not flight or physical integration evidence.
evidence: Monte Carlo simulations were performed with 1000 iterations, ensuring statistical significance in capturing the distribution of possible outcomes.
A 95% confidence level was set for the Monte Carlo analysis.
The sensitivity analysis confirms that even varying in a range of + / - 30%, the subjective part of the model (weights), no significant changes come out of it.
To benchmark and validate the BOREALIS CubeSat design decisions, several existing 6U CubeSat missions were integrated into the model as reference architectures.

items.question: Are requirements, verification, validation, design decisions, or lifecycle gates traced to model artifacts when such traceability is central to the paper?
items.rationale: The process links scientific/mission/system requirement deliverables to ADs, concepts, CONOPS, and subsystem design, but no detailed requirement-to-model or verification trace matrix is shown.
evidence: a Scientific Requirement Document (DEL09) delivered by the biology part of the team presents the main scientific objectives, a Mission Requirement Document (DEL08) collects the high-level and system requirement, and a System Requirement Document (DEL03) deals with the subsystem specifications.
Starting from its results, the degrees of freedom of the system have been identified as architectural decisions (ADs) for the BOREALIS 6U CubeSat.
Development and Verification Plans: Strategic documents that outline the procedures for system validation against the mission requirements and operational readiness checks.

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: A strong system-level CubeSat MBSE case study with detailed context, architecture model, tradespace evidence, and uncertainty analysis. The main weaknesses for this SLR are limited EPS-specific detail, planned rather than demonstrated digital-thread continuity, and incomplete requirement/verification traceability.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as supporting: the paper directly addresses MBSE for a 6U CubeSat mission and includes EPS/power architecture as an architectural decision, but it is not an EPS-specific behavioral modeling or verification study.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Nardi, L.; Carletta, S.; Abbasrezaee, P.; Palmerini, G.; Lovecchio, N.; Burgio, N.; Santagata, A.; Frullini, M.; Calabria, D.; Guardigli, M.; et al. Integrating Model-Based Systems Engineering into CubeSat Development: A Case Study of the BOREALIS Mission. Aerospace 2025, 12, 256. https://doi.org/10.3390/aerospace12030256
bibliographic_review_management.title: Integrating Model-Based Systems Engineering into CubeSat Development: A Case Study of the BOREALIS Mission

RQ1.rationale: The paper models a nanosatellite mission at a general system-architecture level using ADs, MAU/cost functions, and uncertainty analysis; EPS is included only as an electrical power architecture/power-budget decision, not as a detailed EPS behavioral model.

RQ2.rationale: It claims reliability/robustness, reuse/repeatability, and integration/collaboration benefits from MBSE, but these outcomes are system-level and only partly tied to EPS/power modeling.

RQ3.rationale: Development and verification plans are mentioned and the architecture model is checked via tradespace, Monte Carlo, and sensitivity analysis, but the paper does not describe EPS-specific verification procedures integrated into an EPS model before physical development.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: No previous extraction or related papers were consulted due to silo rules. This paper should be treated as a supporting system-level CubeSat MBSE/tradespace study with only power-budget/EPS-architecture relevance.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Apply MBSE systematically to early 6U CubeSat design so mission configurations can be compared quantitatively against performance, cost, risk, and mission constraints rather than relying only on system-engineer intuition.
modeling_scope: Scientific and mission requirements for BOREALIS
Mission profile and CONOPS across LEO, transfer, MEO, decommissioning, and post-operation phases
Architectural decisions for EPS, communications, propulsion, ADCS sensors/actuators, OBC, data handling, thermal control, and software
Ten candidate mission concepts and reference 6U CubeSat architectures
Multi-Attribute Utility and cost model with normalized performance variables and weights
Tradespace/Pareto analysis, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and sensitivity analysis
Planned integrated design model in Excel and Valispace for requirements, budgets, and tracking
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: High-level 6U CubeSat mission and bus architecture, with payload and orbital/radiation constraints included; subsystem choices are abstracted as option-level performance/cost parameters rather than detailed behavioral or electrical designs.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Software AD9 is retained but excluded from the architecture model because it has no effect on the BOREALIS baseline architecture at this stage. The Valispace model is under development and not the article focus. Radiation geometry is preliminary and simplified. EPS is modeled only through power-source options and Wh/kg-style performance, not detailed EPS behavior, control, or verification logic.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Requires mission objectives, mission phases, launch/orbit constraints, COTS subsystem performance/cost/TRL data, propulsion transfer analysis, radiation-dose analysis, and engineering judgment for weights; does not require a detailed dynamic behavior model of each subsystem.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: Uses architectural decisions, normalized performance proxies, subjective but sensitivity-tested weights, reference architecture benchmarks, Monte Carlo uncertainty modeling, and sensitivity analysis to compare designs before detailed subsystem behavior is known.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_lifecycle_gates: The workflow maps scientific objectives to DEL09, mission requirements to DEL08, system engineering planning to DEL04, concept selection and CONOPS to architecture baseline, and subsystem preliminary design to DEL03. Development and Verification Plans are identified as outputs for later validation and operational readiness, but detailed review gates are not shown.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The paper uses MBSE as a model-centered architecture and decision framework enhanced with MAU/cost tradespace analysis, Pareto comparison, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, sensitivity analysis, and planned Valispace continuity. It is not a full formal SysML or demonstrated digital-thread implementation.
tailoring_rationale: 6U CubeSat mass, volume, power, cost, and schedule constraints
Need to move from LEO to MEO while respecting transfer time, TID, and five-year deorbit/decommissioning constraints
Payload requires fluorescence microscopy, lab-on-chip support, radiation shielding, and defined LEO/MEO science windows
Electric/Hall propulsion creates high power and thermal demands that drive EPS and thermal AD choices
Low-cost mission goal encourages COTS use and quantitative comparison of cost/risk/performance trade-offs
Weights and performance metrics are tuned to BOREALIS critical subsystems, especially propulsion and power

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim: The MBSE tradespace model provides quantitative, data-driven support for selecting the BOREALIS baseline architecture rather than relying only on engineering intuition.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.lifecycle_stage: early concept selection and preliminary design
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_type: case-study model results and design-rationale narrative
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.metric_or_value_indicator: Utility versus cost; Concept 10 on/near Pareto-efficient region; comparison with Concepts 7/8 and reference missions
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.baseline_comparator: Traditional engineering intuition, initial preference for Concept 8, and reference CubeSat architectures
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: After adding the Hall-effect-thruster Concept 10, the model showed a performance improvement and supported Concept 10 as baseline.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: The utility/cost model is parameterized by subjective weights and selected concepts; there is no physical or flight validation of the chosen architecture yet.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim: Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses enhance reliability and robustness of the chosen architecture and show that Concept 10 remains resilient under uncertainty.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_or_process_linked: Figures 5, 6, and 7; sensitivity key findings; conclusions
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.metric_or_value_indicator: 1000 Monte Carlo iterations; 95% confidence level; utilities remain within about +/-8% under weight variation; Concept 10 has minimal variability relative to other concepts
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Concept 10 maintained its relative position and Concepts 10 and 8 retained high utility even at minimum variation.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.direct_quote: The integration of sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations added value to the design process, enabling informed decision making and enhancing the reliability of the chosen architecture.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: Uncertainty distributions and weights are author-selected; robustness is in-model only and not yet independently validated by testing.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim: The BOREALIS MBSE workflow is traceable, repeatable, and reusable for future CubeSat missions after retuning architectures, weights, and performance parameters.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.evidence_type: method description with reported equations/data, but no repeated external reuse case
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.baseline_comparator: Unstructured CubeSat design process and author-stated lack of standardized procedures
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Authors argue the workflow supports traceability and repeatability; actual reuse outside BOREALIS is not demonstrated.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.direct_quote: the structured methodology outlined in this paper provides a clear roadmap for correctly implementing the approach.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: Reusability depends on mission-specific retuning and access to the model implementation; no open executable model is reported.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim: A Valispace-based integrated design model will improve integration, real-time updates, collaboration, requirements tracking, and budget continuity across subsystem teams.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.baseline_comparator: Generic document-centric approaches discussed in MBSE background
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Expected collaboration and traceability benefits; not yet implemented or measured in the article.

governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.model_governance_strategy: Governance is organized around program deliverables and planned model continuity: DEL09 for scientific requirements, DEL08 for mission requirements, DEL04 for the system engineering plan, DEL03 for system requirements/subsystem specifications, and a planned Valispace IDM for data, requirements, budgets, and development tracking. Configuration-control details and model ownership/versioning are not reported.
governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.traceability_to_deliverables_decisions_r: The paper traces scientific objectives to mission requirements, constraints, ADs, concept generation, tradespace analysis, concept selection, CONOPS, and preliminary subsystem design. It mentions Development and Verification Plans and system validation against mission requirements, but does not show explicit review-board evidence or a requirement-to-test trace matrix.
governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.evaluation_criteria_model_quality_useful: Model usefulness is evaluated by utility, cost, Pareto efficiency, Monte Carlo uncertainty bars, 95% confidence analysis, +/-30% sensitivity analysis, ranking stability, and comparison against reference 6U CubeSat architectures.
governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.roi_value_realization_evidence: Cost is modeled through hardware, development, launch, operations, and risk costs, and the mission has a low-cost/COTS goal. No realized ROI, schedule saving, budget variance, or post-project economic evidence is reported.
governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.programmatic_gates_critical_design_event: Supports early concept selection, baseline architecture definition, CONOPS, and handoff to preliminary subsystem design/System Requirement Document. Phases A/B shielding work and future verification planning are mentioned; CDR/PDR/TRR use is not detailed.
governance_roi_project_decision_linkage.model_derived_performance_indicators_man: MAU utility, total cost in k€, P_avg, D_rate, propulsion effectiveness E_prop, ADCS accuracy, high-rate ADCS accuracy, OBC processing power, actuator slew rate, data capacity, thermal stability, TRL/risk, transfer time, propellant mass, TID, dose rates, and Pareto/ranking position.

practical_implementation_pathway.rationale: The paper gives a full early-design workflow from requirements and ADs through concept generation, MAU/cost modeling, tradespace analysis, Monte Carlo, sensitivity analysis, and Concept 10 selection, with case-study results.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: It describes Valispace, Excel, GMAT, FLUKA, SPENVIS/IRENE, and centralized data intent, but no formal or demonstrated interoperability mechanism is provided.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The model is tailored to a 6U CubeSat with COTS, mass/volume/power/cost limits, propulsion transfer time, radiation/TID, and low-cost/short-schedule constraints; utility/cost and sensitivity results guide resource prioritization.

governance_project_deliverables_roi_valu.rationale: The study maps requirements and design to ASI deliverables and uses a cost/risk model, but does not report actual ROI, governance metrics, or completed review outcomes.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: The paper emphasizes COTS, low cost, short schedule, real-time Valispace collaboration, and rapid design iteration via tradespace tools, but does not document an agile process or distributed-team iteration cadence.

RQ1: A 6U CubeSat mission can be modeled generally at architecture level by defining subsystem architectural decisions, combining options into mission concepts, and scoring them with normalized utility and cost variables.
EPS is represented minimally as AD1 with power-source options and P_avg performance; detailed EPS behavior, control logic, and electrical interfaces are not modeled.
Limited behavioral knowledge is handled through performance proxies, COTS/reference data, weights, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and sensitivity analysis.
RQ2: Reliability/robustness claims are linked to Monte Carlo and sensitivity evidence showing Concept 10 remains favorable under uncertainty.

Reproducibility/reuse claims are linked to a structured workflow, equations, Appendix data, and statements that the method can be retuned for future CubeSat missions, but no external reuse demonstration is provided.
Integrability claims are mainly prospective, tied to a planned Valispace IDM for real-time collaborative requirements/budget tracking; no implemented integration test evidence is reported.
EPS-specific outcome evidence is limited to the finding that AD1 power subsystem and AD3 propulsion dominate utility variation.
RQ3: No EPS-specific verification procedure is integrated into a detailed EPS model before physical development.

The closest pre-physical verification mechanisms are system-level architecture checks: tradespace/Pareto analysis, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, sensitivity analysis, and reference architecture benchmarking.
Development and Verification Plans are mentioned as future/strategic outputs but not elaborated for EPS.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The Valispace model to manage actual CubeSat data is under development and not the article purpose.
Tools are tailored to BOREALIS and need adaptation, weight reassignment, and possibly performance-parameter changes for other missions.
Weights are subjective and based on engineering judgment, although sensitivity analysis is used to test robustness.
The model is a decision-support tool, not a single source of truth for choosing the concept.
The radiation satellite geometry layout is significantly simplified at this stage and will be detailed as concurrent design proceeds.
A calculation chain for dose during the ascending manoeuvre is under development, so preliminary linear extrapolations are used.
The ten concepts are selected partly by engineering intuition rather than exhaustive enumeration of all combinations.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No formal MBSE language such as SysML is reported.
No open executable model, repository, Valispace workspace, or machine-readable data package is provided.
EPS treatment is limited to power-source architecture and power-performance proxies, not detailed EPS modeling or verification.
Outcome evidence is model-based and preliminary; no integration, environmental test, operational, or flight data validate the MBSE outcomes.
Requirement-to-model-to-verification traceability is described at process level but not demonstrated with a trace matrix or model artifact.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: Emphasis will be given to the model built for the tradeoff analysis, explaining how it was built and used and providing the reader with all the elements to possibly reuse it for another mission design of the same satellite class.

Regarding the design process, starting from the scientific objectives of the mission, the mission requirements and constraints have been identified to understand the possible choice on each satellite subsystem for the CubeSat configuration.
AD1 Electric Power System Body Mounted Solar Array(2×6U+2×3U) Large Deployable Solar Array Deployable Solar ArrayHigh-capacity Batteries
In the context of the BOREALIS mission, MBSE has been integral to aligning complex biological and engineering requirements within the constraints of a CubeSat platform.
It is worth mentioning that the model under development on Valispace to manage the actual CubeSat data is not the purpose of this article.
The model incorporates normalized data for each variable based on the performance of each subsystem in the reference mission concept [Annex A].
Monte Carlo simulations were performed with 1000 iterations, ensuring statistical significance in capturing the distribution of possible outcomes.
The analysis confirmed the dominance of AD1 (power subsystem) and AD3 (propulsion system) as the most impactful parameters across all concepts.
This case exemplifies how the MBSE approach can not only validate engineering intuition but also provides insights that can lead to better-informed design choices.

By integrating parametrized tradespace evaluation, Monte Carlo and sensitivity analysis into the system engineering process, this study demonstrated the effectiveness of a data-driven approach to guide the satellite configuration.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: Treat as supporting evidence for MBSE-enabled nanosatellite architecture selection and power-budget/EPS-architecture trade studies, not as a core EPS behavioral modeling or EPS verification study. No lineage comparison was performed under the silo rules.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The full Markdown paper was read and the relevant MBSE, mission, EPS-architecture, and verification-related details are explicit. Confidence is lower only for EPS-specific synthesis because the paper itself provides limited EPS detail.
